reconstructed_theorem_text: For all measurable spaces W and Omega, with singleton subsets of W measurable, any data measure P on Omega, any natural N>0, w:Fin N->W, K:W->Omega->R, and label:Omega->R, assume each sampled slice K(w(i)) and label belong to L2(P) in the MemLp sense. Define rho=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_i dirac(w(i)) on W. Then rho is a probability measure; omega->(integral_W K(q,omega) drho(q)-label(omega))^2 is genuinely Bochner integrable under P; and its real integral under P equals norm_{L2(P)}((N:R)^(-1) times sum_i [K(w(i))]-[label])^2, where brackets are the toLp classes from the supplied memberships. The actual inner integral equals (N:R)^(-1)*sum_i K(w(i),omega) for every omega. Thus prediction is averaged before subtraction and squaring. P itself is arbitrary and need not have finite mass or be a probability. Fin N has N indices; w need not be injective and an atom with multiplicity m has mass m/N. No global measurability of K or L2 membership of nonsampled slices is imposed. The L2 equality is an equality involving equivalence classes, whose chosen representatives agree with the raw functions only almost everywhere.
objects: W,Omega; arbitrary data measure P; positive N; indexed particles w; real kernel K and label; actual empirical measure rho; actual predictor; sampled feature and label L2(P) classes.
domains: W and Omega are measurable spaces, and W singletons are measurable. P:Measure Omega is arbitrary. N:N with N>0; w:Fin N->W; K:W->Omega->R; label:Omega->R. rho is a measure on W; L2 norm and outer integral use P.
quantifiers: Universally quantify the spaces, P,N>0,w,K,label. For every sampled index i assume MemLp(K(w(i)),2,P), and assume MemLp(label,2,P). Define rho once and conclude the three claims for these choices.
assumptions: Supplied: measurable singletons of W, positive N, L2 membership of every sampled slice and label. No distinct-particle condition, global kernel measurability, probability condition on P, or pre-assumed squared-residual integrability.
conclusion: rho has total mass one; the actual prediction residual squared is P-integrable; its real P-integral equals the squared norm of the averaged sampled-feature L2(P) classes minus the label class.
scopes: rho is on W and governs the inner integral; P is on Omega and governs data membership, the outer integral, and the L2 norm. Measurable singletons and finite atomic support permit the actual pointwise prediction average without global kernel measurability. Repeated values accumulate their index weights. Averaging occurs inside the square; the loss is unhalved. Chosen L2 representatives need agree with raw functions only P-almost everywhere. N=0 is excluded.
constant_dependencies: Each index has exactly weight 1/N via the displayed measure and real scalar inverses. There is no normalization of P, additional risk constant, or factor 1/2.
